injuries.summary:
**Today's NFL injury briefing**

League roster deadlines are driving a lot of the movement: teams are finalizing cuts, practice squads, and IR-return designations.

**Biggest status changes**
- **Washington**: the Commanders’ top cornerback will **miss Week 1 vs. the Eagles**. That’s a clear early advantage for Philadelphia’s passing game.
- **Cleveland**: **Dillon Gabriel** was placed on **injured reserve** on Sunday. **Taylen Green** is now the Browns’ No. 3 QB for at least the first month.
- **Las Vegas**: third-round pick **Keyron Crawford** was placed on **season-ending IR**.
- **Atlanta**: LB **Bralen Trice** was waived after spending both of his first two seasons on IR without playing a game.

**Players returning / eligible to return**
- **Adam Randall** was placed on **IR with a designation to return** and will miss at least the first four weeks.
- **Houston**: **Tank Dell** and **Ja’Marcus Ingram** were designated to return.
- In the 49ers WR notes, **Christian Kirk** is listed as **calf / IR-return**.
- **Ricky Pearsall** is **out for the year** with a PCL injury.

**Other notable injury designations**
- **Chargers**: undrafted T **Isaiah World** was placed on the **reserve/non-football injury list** after an ACL tear.
- **Mykel Williams** was placed on the **PUP list**.
- **Charbonnet** was placed on **PUP** to start the season.
- **Brett Toth** and **Nick Zakelj** were placed on **IR** and are **not** designated to return.

**Texans roster churn tied to injuries**
- RB **Jawhar Jordan** was released healthy after recovering from a strained hip flexor.
- **Noah Whittington** is expected to join the practice squad.
- **E.J. Speed** and **M.J. Stewart** are starting camp on **PUP**.
- **Ali Gaye** is on **IR**.
- **Solomon Byrd** and **Kyonte Hamilton** were waived-injured; **Alijah Huzzie** and **Derek Parish** were waived.

**What to watch next**
- Final IR-return and practice-squad moves after the roster deadline window.
- Whether Washington’s CB absence changes the Week 1 matchup.
- How quickly **Dell**, **Ingram**, **Randall**, and **Christian Kirk** can get back.

sources.title: Today, teams can claim players off waivers up to 10AM (PT). After NFL wire goes out, teams may establish their practices squads of 17 players (as long as one is an international player). Beginning at 1 p.m., any player placed on injured reserve may be designated for return.
Commanders’ top cornerback will miss Week 1 against the Eagles

Falcons LB Bralen Trice was a 3rd-round pick in 2024 and tore ACL in first preseason game. Aggravated injury in 2025. On IR both seasons and played no games either year. Was waived Sunday. What a horrible pick by them.

I know I’m supposed to be objective and what not, but man, this whole thing is just so damn cool to me. I was lucky enough to cover Donald’s first five seasons day to day and he truly is 1 of 1. The league is better just by having him back in it. Can’t wait to see how it unfolds.

A surprise: Adam Randall has been placed on injured reserve to open the season with a designation to return. He looked fine talking to reporters after the game, but he'll miss at least the first four weeks. https://t.co/inI9WXkizc
Chargers placed undrafted T Isaiah World on the reserve/non-football injury list. The Oregon product tore his ACL in the playoff game against Indiana.

26 of Omar Khan's 31 draft picks since taking over as GM before the 2023 team are currently on the roster (Broderick Jones, Kaleb Johnson, Cory Trice, Logan Lee, Ryan Watts). Trice, Lee and Watts were late-round picks who suffered injuries.

Over last 23 years, 33 undrafted rookies have made Baltimore’s initial 53-man roster. 🏈Two reserves are placed on IR/Designated to Return: CB Bilhal Kone and RB Adam Randall. Baltimore can designate six more players to return off IR for the rest of the season. 🏈Two players from 2026 draft class were waived (both 7th-rounders): DL Rayshaun Benny and OL Evan Beerntsen. From the 2026 draft, eight picks made the 53-man roster and one (Randall) was placed on IR. 🏈Ravens keep 3 QBs (Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano) for first time since 2023. 🏈Two trades: DT C.J. Okoye (to Giants) and OT Diego Pounds (to Chiefs). Ravens gain a 2028 seventh-round pick for Okoye and a conditional 2028 sixth-rounder for Pounds. 🏈Of the 33 players waived/released, five were former Ravens draft picks: Benny, Beerntsen, OLB Adisa Isaac (3rd round in 2024), CB Robert Longerbeam (6th round in 2025) and WR Chris Moore (4th round in 2016). 🏈Ravens can start signing players to 17-player practice squad after 1PM ET on Monday.

Some Patriots thoughts/news nuggets: 🏈This was a straight-forward cut-down day. No shocking moves. One of the more interesting decisions was keeping quarterback Behren Morton, the 2026 seventh-round pick from Texas Tech, as the third option. It speaks to the importance of the position; notable that four teams kept four QBs on initial 53-man rosters (Eagles, Falcons, Steelers, Vikings), which is unusual. 🏈Would be shocked if the Patriots don’t aggressively address OLB, either on the practice squad or a waiver claim. Teams aren’t giving quality pass-rushers away, but a player like Caleb Murphy – who played five games for the Patriots last season, was waived by the Giants, and would be a plug-and-play core special teamer at minimum – would provide the team with some much-needed experienced OLB depth. 🏈Five. That’s the number of players I believe would have been on the initial 53-man roster if not for injuries and it’s a reminder that when the topic of the Patriots’ lack of depth is broached, it is as much about health as it is shaky drafting. That list includes OT Marcus Bryant, TE Julian Hill, OLB Harold Landry III, RB Terrell Jennings and ST Brenden Schooler. 🏈Veteran punter Mitch Wishnowsky is a target for the Patriots with incumbent Bryce Baringer still sidelined due to an undisclosed lower-body injury. The expectation is Wishnowsky will be in town for a physical soon. Wouldn't surprise me if that moves quickly. 🏈NT Cory Durden was a waiver claim at this time last year and he has become an important cog for the team. One thing that has been apparent: Because the Patriots are No. 31 in the waiver-claim order this year, instead of No. 4 last year, they’ve been more aggressive with trades for RB Corey Kiner (Cardinals) and T/G Walter Rouse (Vikings) to fill depth roles. So Kiner is the early leading candidate to be this year's Durden. 🏈On Rouse (6-6, 330), he was a tackle up until training camp this year, when the Vikings began experimenting with him at guard. He falls into the Bill Parcells category of “looks good coming off the bus” player. Rouse, who played at Stanford and Oklahoma and entered the NFL as a 2024 sixth-round pick of the Vikings, has said he hopes to be a doctor.

Here are 10 thoughts on the Commanders' initial 53-man roster: 1) It's obvious that Fabian Moreau is going to be back on the team as soon as Trey Amos hits IR. WSH only has three healthy CB's on the 53 until Moreau is brought back, but he's vested and doesn't need to clear waivers so he isn't at risk of being claimed. 2) Speaking of Amos -- the IR news is bad. That means he's going to miss 4 games. That's your CB1 in a fairly pedestrian CB room. What is going on with Amos? Putting him on IR is an indicator that he's still weeks away from practicing at game speed. How did we get here? 3) The center position continues to flummox me. Julian Good-Jones went from "competing for the starting spot" to cut in the span of a few weeks. Matt Gulbin went from a rough joint practice against Baltimore to the only healthy guy on the team at the position in days. Clearly Nick Allegretti is due back soon but I'm stunned a veteran hasn't been added yet. That will undoubtedly happen tomorrow. 4) Athan Kaliakmanis as QB3 is a clear endorsement of how well he played in the preseason, namely against Detroit. He showed a little too much for the Commanders to feel like they could get him on the practice squad. My guess is they could have gotten him to the taxi group but they were not willing to risk it. 5) The 7th WR spot came down to Luke McCaffrey and Van Jefferson. I like the decision to keep McCaffrey even though Jefferson is the better WR right now. So why keep Luke? Well he's younger, has more upside, helps on special teams and is under contract for longer. WSH already has several WR's on expiring deals (Diggs, Burks, Brown) and Terry McLaurin may even be in his final year with the team pending the results of the 2026 campaign. It makes sense to layer the roster with more players who have more term remaining like McCaffrey. 6) The DT spot ended up being super deep and very competitive. I thought Byron Cowart and Maurice Hurst were both good enough to make the squad. Same with Shy Tuttle, although I think he'll rejoin the team as soon as Johnny Newton hits IR. Like Moreau, he's vested and doesn't need to go through the waivers process. I think the Commanders are well put on the interior up front. 7) Speaking of roster spots I like -- I really think Adam Peters did a nice job with the edge, off-ball linebacker, tight end and wide receiver spots. 8) I'm surprised Ale Kaho got cut. I would have kept him on the 53 as a 6th LB. He is good on special teams and he could've helped Kain Medrano and Jordan Magee as anchors on teams and depth backers. He'll likely end up on the practice squad and stay in the building. 9) The CB room gives me anxiety. Mike Sainristil needs to have a much better season than he did last year. With Amos out, Sainristil will be counted on to help anchor the position on the outside. The Cowboys loom in Week 2 and that meeting with George Pickens and Ceedee Lamb is going to be a massive test for WSH's pass rush. They'll need to protect the corner room. 10) Speaking of the Commanders' pass rush, Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson have both been battling injuries and haven't practiced in weeks. The Commanders defense has a chance to be massively improved but only if those two guys can be healthy and prolific.

LV.summary:
- **Jeanty (RB)** — Las Vegas kept only three running backs, which suggests Jeanty’s injury is not expected to keep him out long, strong trust in Washington, or both. That keeps Washington in the early-down mix and could make Laube more important on returns while Jeanty is sidelined, so every back snap carries added fantasy weight. [6]

- **Kirk Cousins (QB)** — Cousins is set to open the season as the Raiders’ starter, with Fernando Mendoza developing behind him and Aidan O’Connell next up. The Raiders and Klint Kubiak have leaned veteran from the start, which pushes Mendoza into a stash-and-wait role rather than an early-season fantasy option. [6, 7, 9, 11]

- **Tre Tucker (WR)** — The Raiders still do not have many established receivers beyond Tucker, with the room described as a concern and no true standouts other than him. If that holds, Tucker is the best bet to benefit from target concentration, though the rest of the pecking order is not specified. [8]

- **Matt Gay (K)** — Gay won the kicking job after the Raiders waived Kansei Matsuzawa. He now has the inside track to all the team’s scoring chances, though the note says his job security could still be week-to-week if he struggles. [12]

- **Carsen Ryan (FB/TE)** — Among the rest of the rookie class, he’s viewed as the best bet for early playing time because of what he can do in the run game.
